faqs.q: Are AI video maker apps free to use?
faqs.a: Many AI video and art tools offer a free plan or trial, but it usually comes with limits such as watermarks, lower resolution, fewer exports or restricted features. Paid plans remove most of these limits, so check what the free version includes before relying on it for regular or commercial work.

faqs.q: Can I use AI-generated videos for YouTube or business?
faqs.a: Generally yes, but check two things first. The tool's licence terms decide whether you may use its output commercially, and the platform's own rules may ask you to label realistic AI-generated content and may not reward low-effort, mass-produced videos.

faqs.q: Who owns the copyright of AI-generated art or video?
faqs.a: It is not fully settled. Ownership depends on the tool's terms of service and on copyright law, which in India and many other countries does not yet clearly protect work made entirely by AI without meaningful human input. Adding your own script, editing and creative choices strengthens your claim, and for important commercial work it is worth taking legal advice.

faqs.q: Will AI video tools replace video editors?
faqs.a: Not entirely. AI tools speed up routine tasks such as cutting clips, adding captions, colour correction and generating visuals, but storytelling, judgement and a consistent style still depend on people. Editors who learn to use AI tools are more likely to work faster than to be replaced outright.
